design_rationale:
WORKLOG / DOSSIER — task 0 (pharmacy_prescription_care, env_0040_pet_supplies_retailer)

[Step 0 — draw and scope] draw_counts.py --task 0 printed {"prerequisite_problems": 1, "problems": 2, "factor_counts": [4, 5]}. Tree = 2 problems: root rx_ext_controlled_renewal (4 factors) <- rx_ext_error_refund (5 factors). Occupied before this task: nothing (first task). This task claims the controlled-substance customer renewal (rx_order_create, owner=user) and the mandatory dispensing-error refund for classes without a free remake (rx_error_refund + rx_fill_restore, owner=agent). Left for task 1 (draw 1 prerequisite, factor counts [5, 6]) and later claimed there: the pharmacy-placed renewal of auto-renewal classes and the household new order for a prescription diet; both policies here are scoped (controlled class / error_remake_allowed false) so task 1 keeps an independent space, and task 1 writes no refund entry, keeping this task's state-form sentence single-writer.

[Why a good test] The customer asks only for a renewal of Juniper's phenobarbital. The renewal's fill length is a 4-factor computation (Autoship cadence method, stability, adherence and exhaustion ceilings), and the renewal policy's own rule says its result 'is fixed only after every dispensed fill of the renewed prescription that carries a dispensing-error claim also carries a refund entry on the pharmacy ledger'. The ledger shows the 2026-09-24 fill with error_type wrong_strength and no refund entry, so the agent must discover, from the refund policy, that its write books exactly that refund entry, price the refund (5 factors, two read from the Pals Rewards membership), book it, and only then compute the renewal on the settled ledger and hand the renewal order to the customer. Difficulty comes from reading the prerequisite sentence, reconciling six fills, reading two other products (Autoship, membership) and getting two numbers exact; tools are unambiguous.

[Problem-tree card] root rx_ext_controlled_renewal (target place_rx_renewal_order_580a75e8, owner=user, on_request). Edge -> rx_ext_error_refund: kind value_input, gate claims_open, form state, prerequisite sentence (affirmative direction, this is how a pharmacy states that a figure waits on the ledger being settled): 'The days' supply per fill a renewal order asks for is fixed only after every dispensed fill of the renewed prescription that carries a dispensing-error claim also carries a refund entry on the pharmacy ledger.' Four-point test: ordering connective 'only after'; record-visible state (a refund entry against each claimed fill); no tool, id or code token; strength 'every ... claimed fill', exactly the condition. Exactly one write of the difficulty books refund entries on a controlled prescription: refund_dispensing_error_93fa9db7 (the refund policy's rule: 'the refund is paid to the original payment, and the refunded fill is credited back'). Derivation: sentence + ledger (fill 6 wrong_strength, no rx_error_refund row) + refund rule -> the refund write. Seed evidence of falsity: initial_state.rx_events.b63b7557-....error_type = wrong_strength, no rx_events row with original_event_id = that fill. Resolved by the agent synchronously. Topological order: refund (step 7) then renewal (step 11). Deletion sensitivity (run): skipping the refund leaves claims_open = 1, stability ceiling 14, days_supply_per_fill 14 (gold 28) and no refund/credit-back rows. user_scenario never mentions the claim; tools validate nothing (see prerequisite_closure).

[Factor card — refund (expected 37.56, baseline 20.53)] Claimed fill = latest rx_fill (2026-09-24): merchandise 10.08 (28 x 0.36), discount 0.00, shipping 4.95, service 5.50 (adult signature), billed 20.53, wrong_strength => severe. courtesy_basis (method, multi-source: severe AND fills in 12 months): 6 fills >= 4 -> courtesy on the billed 20.53 (baseline: no courtesy -> 34.48). courtesy_percentage (parameter, cross-difficulty member): Pals Rewards VIP active -> 15% (baseline 0 -> 34.48); courtesy = RND(3.0795) = 3.08. replacement_shipping (parameter): severe AND one_time_order -> 4.95 + 4.95 = 9.90 (baseline 4.95 -> 32.61). loyalty_makegood (parameter, cross-difficulty member): enrolled 2017-09-12, 108 whole months >= 96 -> 5.00 (near miss: tier_effective_on 2026-01-01 is not the enrollment date; baseline 0 -> 32.56). waiting_credit (parameter, multi-source: severe AND days since the claimed fill): 12 days >= 10 -> 4.00 (baseline 0 -> 33.56). The service fee charged (5.50) enters as read. Sum 10.08 + 9.90 + 5.50 + 3.08 + 5.00 + 4.00 = 37.56. Overwrite declared: base rx_dispensing_errors sentence 'A refund returns the fill's merchandise amount after discount and, with error_refund_includes_shipping, its shipping and service fees, to the original payment, and the refunded fill is credited back to fills_remaining.' replaced by the policy's sum sentence (service fee and credit-back kept). Base gates error_window and one_remedy_per_error stay inherited.

[Factor card — renewal (expected 21, baseline 14)] delivery_rhythm (method, cross-difficulty autoship, multi-source): Autoship Pharmacy 132438e0-... linked to the prescription, status pending_first_shipment (enrolled 2026-09-20 while one fill remained), 4 weeks -> 28. stability_ceiling (parameter, multi-source; the value_input gate): after the refund 0 open claims and 6 - 1 = 5 delivered -> 30; before it the open claim gives 14 (near miss: fill 6 still carries error_type wrong_strength; the refund entry against it closes the claim). adherence_ceiling (parameter): days' supply dispensed net of credit-backs (the base measure rx_msr_days_supply_dispensed) = 84 - 14 = 70 over 85 days since 2026-07-13 = 82.35%, in [75, 90) with 6 fills -> 14 + 7 = 21 (near miss: counting the credited-back fill gives 98.8% and 30). exhaustion_ceiling (parameter): refills_exhausted, 111 days from closed_on 2026-09-24 to expires_on 2027-01-13 >= 30 -> 30. result = int(MN(28, 30, 21, 30, 30)) = 21; quantity 21 x 28/14 = 42. Every factor substituted by its baseline gives 14. overwrite [] (base renewal rules say nothing on fill length; base gates one_live_rx_per_medication, dea_prescriber, shippable_state, current_weight inherited; rx_evt_fill_eligibility cited as the lineage of the net days' supply measure).

[Base-invariant card] Refund: error_window (time; anchor rx_events.event_date of the erroneous fill, day 0 = 2026-09-24, 14 calendar days inclusive -> last day 2026-10-08; frozen 2026-10-06 = day 12, in time; 2026-10-09 would be late). one_remedy_per_error: no rx_error_remake/rx_error_refund row refers to fill 6. Renewal: one_live_rx_per_medication — the only Phenobarbital 64.8 mg tablet prescription for Juniper is refills_exhausted, none pending/active; dea_prescriber — Dr. Priya Raman dea_registered true; shippable_state — MN not in AK/HI/NV; current_weight (time; order date 2026-10-06, 6 months back = 2026-04-06 inclusive) — weight recorded 2026-07-15 is current.

[Business-object card] Target object of the refund: fill b63b7557-aa65-4fbb-a733-8c7b9ff99e5c (fill_number 6) of prescription 318efa8f-...; correlation key original_event_id. Fills 1-5 (2026-07-13..09-06, error_type none) are excluded from the refund and only feed counts. Renewal object: prescription 318efa8f-... (renewal_of_rx_id), same pet/medication/strength/vet. No earlier reversal exists.

[World rows] customers (identity + MN), pets (weight date for the gate), veterinarians (DEA), rx_prescriptions (renewed prescription; every ceiling reads it), rx_events x6 (claim, refund inputs, counts, coverage), autoship_subscriptions (cadence factor), member_memberships (two refund factors). Removing the autoship row drops the renewal to 14; removing the membership drops the refund by 8.08 (courtesy 3.08 + make-good 5.00); removing fill 6's claim removes the tree. No automatic clause is lit: the Autoship's next ship date is 2026-10-22 (no hold yet), the prescription is exhausted not expired, controlled renewals are never auto-placed (auto_renewal_request false), the membership has no fees due.

[Persona] Dolores Fairbanks, polite and a little anxious; volunteers only the renewal request; gives mobile 6515550231 then ZIP 55105 when asked (email and card ending 2735 only if more is needed); names Dr. Raman; mentions the 4-week Autoship only when asked about deliveries; agrees to anything Tailwise must sort out first and to refunds to the original card; reacts to a refund only after the agent announces it; accepts the days/tablets she is told; places the renewal herself when handed the tool; ends once it is placed. No prerequisite, number or policy is in her mouth.

[Standard solution, executed] Reads: find_customers -> verify (phone + ZIP) -> find_pets -> find_rx_prescriptions -> find_rx_events -> find_member_memberships; unlock + call refund_dispensing_error_93fa9db7 {rx_prescription_id 318efa8f-..., original_event_id b63b7557-..., error_type wrong_strength, amount_usd 37.56}; find_veterinarians -> find_autoship_subscriptions; unlock_user + call_user place_rx_renewal_order_580a75e8 {..., days_supply_per_fill 21, quantity_per_fill 42}. Gates run on this file: check_extended --task 0 EXTENDED OK; check_task_tools TASK TOOL CONTRACT OK; replay_tasks --task 0 REPLAY OK (12/12 rows closed); check_solvability --task 0 SOLVABILITY OK (8 base gates); check_compute --task 0 COMPUTE OK (2 comps, 9 factors, 3 cross-difficulty, recompute 37.56 and 21, every factor_sensitivity matched); check_grounding GROUNDING OK; check_cross_fire SCOPE OK.

[Draft recomputation from visible context] From the published renewal rule the agent reads that the fill length waits on refund entries for claimed fills; the ledger read shows the wrong_strength claim; the refund rule prices it from the fill row, the class parameters and the membership record (VIP, 2017 enrollment) -> 37.56; after the refund the ledger shows 0 open claims, 5 delivered fills and 70 net days dispensed; the Autoship record gives 28, the adherence ceiling 21, the other ceilings 30 -> 21 days, 42 tablets. Same as gold. Mistakes a careful reader excludes: computing the renewal first (14), counting the credited-back fill in the days dispensed (28), taking courtesy on merchandise only (35.99), counting tenure from tier_effective_on (32.56), dropping the replacement shipping cover (32.61).

[Closure] policies {rx_ext_error_refund, rx_ext_controlled_renewal} -> tools {refund_dispensing_error_93fa9db7 (agent), place_rx_renewal_order_580a75e8 (user)} -> computations steps 7 and 11 -> terminal state: refund + credit-back rows, fills_remaining 1 on the exhausted prescription, new pending renewal prescription with 21 days / 42 tablets. required_documents = charter_scope.extended_policies.

[Revision round 2 — policy-task audit] F1/T0-1 (days' supply dispensed defined gross, base measure rx_msr_days_supply_dispensed is net): the adherence (and task 1's coverage) sentence now defines the quantity as the base measure does, 'the days' supply of its dispensed fills less the days' supply of the fills credited back to it'; compute subtracts SUM(days_supply) of rx_fill_restore rows; the refund tool now writes the credited fill's days_supply on the credit-back row; rx_evt_fill_eligibility added to base_policy_refs as lineage. Re-run: adherence 70/85 = 82.35% -> 21, renewal 28 -> 21 days, 56 -> 42 tablets; the second reading no longer exists. F2/T0-2 (replacement_service_fee could not divide in-scope customers, tier 2 unreachable): factor removed; the service fee charged now enters as a plain read; replaced by waiting_credit (severe AND days from the claimed fill's dispense date to the refund date: >= 10 -> 4.00, 5..9 -> 2.00, else 0), whose tiers are all reachable inside the 14-day report window. Refund 39.06 -> 37.56. T0-O2: Autoship enrollment moved to 2026-09-20, while the prescription still had one fill. T0-O5: the delivery_rhythm 'near miss' claim was dropped; the near misses are the refunded claimed fill (stability) and the credited-back fill (adherence). Gates re-run green (see the final block in the worklog of task 1).
user_scenario: You are Dolores Fairbanks, a 61-year-old retired school librarian in Saint Paul, Minnesota, calling Tailwise Pet Co. about Juniper, your Border Collie mix, who has epilepsy and takes phenobarbital twice a day. The Tailwise app now says her prescription has no refills left, so you open by saying that Juniper's seizure medicine has run out of refills and you need a renewal ordered with her vet, and that you want it taken care of on this call. You are friendly but a little anxious, and you speak in full, polite sentences. When the representative asks how to find your account you give your mobile number, which you read out as 6515550231. When they ask for something more to confirm it is you, you give your billing ZIP code, 55105; only if they still need another detail do you add your email, dolores.fairbanks@gmail.com, or that the card on file ends in 2735. Juniper is the only pet on your account, and her vet is Dr. Priya Raman at Como Lake Veterinary Clinic; you want the renewal to go to Dr. Raman. Only when the representative asks about deliveries do you mention that last month you set Juniper's pills up on Autoship every four weeks so they just keep coming. You are glad for the representative to look over the account and take care of anything on Tailwise's side that the renewal needs; if they tell you something has to be sorted out first, you tell them to go ahead, and if money is coming back to you, you say it should go back to the card it was paid with. If the representative tells you they are refunding your most recent bottle, you thank them warmly and say you remember reporting in the app that those tablets looked different from Juniper's usual ones; you do not question the amount. When the representative tells you how many days per fill and how many tablets the renewal will ask Dr. Raman for, you accept it. You would rather place the renewal order yourself, so once the representative hands the renewal order over to you, you place it exactly as they set it up and read back the confirmation it shows. As soon as the renewal is placed and on its way to Dr. Raman you thank the representative and end the call. You never bring up anything about earlier bottles on your own, you ask for nothing beyond the renewal, and if asked whether there is anything else, you say no, that is everything.

A prescription that is refills_exhausted or expired is continued only through a renewal, a new prescription with origin renewal and renewal_of_rx_id pointing at the old one; for classes without auto_renewal_request the customer asks for it.

temporal_feasibility.condition: A dispensing error is accepted only if it is reported no later than dispensing_error_report_days after the erroneous fill's dispense date.

temporal_basis.counting_rule: The window is counted in calendar days from the event_date of the erroneous rx_fill row, that date being day 0; a report on the last day is in time.

boundary_check.just_before: Rx Controlled Substance dispensing_error_report_days is 14; counting from 2026-09-24 as day 0, a report on 2026-10-09 (day 15) would be refused.
boundary_check.at_boundary: Day 14 is 2026-10-08, still in time (inclusive); frozen_time 2026-10-06 is day 12, so the claim is in time.

temporal_feasibility.condition: When weight_check_required is true, the pet's weight is checked only if it was recorded no earlier than weight_record_max_age_months before the order date.

temporal_basis.counting_rule: The weight age is counted in calendar months back from the order date, falling back to the last day of the month when that day does not exist; a weight recorded exactly on that boundary date is current.

boundary_check.just_before: weight_record_max_age_months is 6 for Rx Controlled Substance; with the order date 2026-10-06 the boundary is 2026-04-06, so a weight recorded 2026-04-05 would not be current.
boundary_check.at_boundary: A weight recorded exactly on 2026-04-06 is current (inclusive); Juniper's weight of 2026-07-15 is well inside the window.

argument_uniqueness_tracing.rx_prescription_id: Value 318efa8f-029f-429c-94f0-162a3feaea9b. Basis: the prescription lookup returns one prescription for the customer (Phenobarbital 64.8 mg tablet), and the claimed fill's ledger row carries rx_prescription_id 318efa8f-029f-429c-94f0-162a3feaea9b. Uniqueness: the customer holds no other prescription, so no other reference number is reachable.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.original_event_id: Value b63b7557-aa65-4fbb-a733-8c7b9ff99e5c. Basis: the refund policy rule 'It covers a claim recorded on the most recent dispensed fill of a prescription, and that fill is the claimed fill'; the ledger row dated 2026-09-24 (fill_number 6) is the most recent rx_fill row and the only one whose error_type is not none. Uniqueness: the five earlier fills carry error_type none, so they are not claimed fills.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.error_type: Value wrong_strength. Basis: the claimed fill row's error_type field reads wrong_strength, and the tool docstring defines wrong_strength as 'the right medication was dispensed at a strength or formula other than the prescribed one'. Uniqueness: the refund records the error being remedied, which is the one recorded on the claimed fill; wrong_medication, wrong_quantity and wrong_label are not what the record shows, and none never describes a refund.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.amount_usd: Value 37.56. Merchandise portion: claimed fill merchandise 10.08 less discount 0.00 = 10.08. Shipping portion (replacement_shipping): severe claim and one_time_order fill -> fill shipping 4.95 + Rx Controlled Substance rx_shipping_fee_usd 4.95 = 9.90. Service fee charged on the fill: 5.50. Courtesy (courtesy_basis + courtesy_percentage): six fills dated within 12 months >= 4 -> figured on the whole billed amount 20.53; Pals Rewards VIP active -> 15 percent; 20.53 x 0.15 = 3.0795 -> 3.08 rounded half up. Loyalty make-good: membership enrolled 2017-09-12, 108 whole months to 2026-10-06 >= 96 -> 5.00. Waiting credit: severe claim, DAYS(2026-09-24, 2026-10-06) = 12 >= 10 -> 4.00. Sum 10.08 + 9.90 + 5.50 + 3.08 + 5.00 + 4.00 = 37.56.

argument_uniqueness_tracing.pet_id: Value 9a146793-bcb0-4f19-9363-7c8181d1ceaa. Basis: the renewed prescription's pet_id and the pet lookup (Juniper, the only pet). Uniqueness: a renewal is for the same pet as the prescription it renews (rx_agg_multi_holding / rx_renewals).

argument_uniqueness_tracing.renewal_of_rx_id: Value 318efa8f-029f-429c-94f0-162a3feaea9b. Basis: rx_renewals 'a new prescription with origin renewal and renewal_of_rx_id pointing at the old one'. Uniqueness: the only refills_exhausted prescription of the customer.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.days_supply_per_fill: Value 21. Delivery rhythm: linked Autoship Pharmacy subscription in status pending_first_shipment, 4 weeks x 7 = 28 <= class maximum 30 -> fill length 28. Stability ceiling (after the refund): no open claim (one wrong_strength claim, one refund entry) and fills delivered 6 - 1 credit-back = 5 >= 5 -> 30. Adherence ceiling: days' supply dispensed net of fills credited back = 84 - 14 = 70 over 85 calendar days from 2026-07-13 to 2026-10-06 = 82.35 percent, at least 75 but below 90 with 6 >= 4 fills -> 14 + 7 = 21. edges.condition: Every rx_events row of event_type rx_fill on the renewed prescription whose error_type is other than none is referred to, through original_event_id, by an rx_events row of event_type rx_error_refund on the same prescription, which comes with its rx_fill_restore credit-back row.
edges.policy_source: The days' supply per fill a renewal order asks for is fixed only after every dispensed fill of the renewed prescription that carries a dispensing-error claim also carries a refund entry on the pharmacy ledger.

unresolved_at_frozen_time.why_false: The 2026-09-24 fill carries a wrong_strength claim and the prescription's ledger holds no refund entry referring to it, so a claimed fill lacks its refund entry at frozen_time.
evidence: initial_state.rx_events.b63b7557-aa65-4fbb-a733-8c7b9ff99e5c.rx_event_id = b63b7557-aa65-4fbb-a733-8c7b9ff99e5c (no rx_error_refund row refers to it)
unresolved_at_frozen_time.flips_to_true_by: The refund call books an rx_error_refund row with original_event_id b63b7557-aa65-4fbb-a733-8c7b9ff99e5c and an rx_fill_restore row carrying its 14 days, so the open-claim count becomes 0 and fills delivered become 5; the stability ceiling moves from 14 to 30 and the renewal's days' supply from 14 to 21.

prerequisite_closure.order_uniqueness: Single edge, no parallel prerequisites: the refund must land before the renewal is computed because the renewal's prerequisite sentence ('fixed only after every dispensed fill of the renewed prescription that carries a dispensing-error claim also carries a refund entry') states the order; the refund's own computation reads nothing the renewal writes, so the order is fixed by the edge alone.

edge_load_bearing.skipped_effect: Skipping the refund leaves claims_open = 1, the stability ceiling falls to the renewed prescription's 14 days and days_supply_per_fill becomes 14 instead of 21 (quantity 28 instead of 42); the terminal state also lacks the rx_error_refund and rx_fill_restore rows and keeps fills_remaining 0.

prerequisite_closure.no_user_hint: user_scenario raises only the renewal. It never mentions the claim, a refund or the last bottle on its own; the only reference to the earlier bottle sits inside a reaction that fires after the representative says they are refunding the most recent bottle, and the customer explicitly never brings up earlier bottles on her own.
prerequisite_closure.tools_do_not_block: place_rx_renewal_order_580a75e8 reads only the renewed prescription to copy its class, item number and price and creates the pending renewal with whatever days and packages it is given; it never checks open claims, refunds or fills. refund_dispensing_error_93fa9db7 books its rows without checking windows or duplicates.
